name: Orvana Occasion Gown — Wing-Slit Standard
description:
Orvana's formal gown line has long offered geneware-accommodation as standard rather than as an upsell, which is part of why the brand has maintained loyalty among modified clientele. The Wing-Slit Standard is a floor-length gown in a structured silk-analog with a built-in dorsal panel system — two reinforced slit channels running from mid-shoulder-blade to hip, framed in a contrasting bias-cut trim that makes the openings appear intentional rather than accommodating. For clients with non-functional decorative wings, the slits allow the geneware to present naturally without bunching or compressing the fabric. Tail accommodation is standard at the rear hem. The gown is available in eight colorways and accepts bioluminescent trim as an add-on service.

The price point sits at the upper end of Tier 3, making it aspirational for some and routine for others. It is a garment for people who have modified their bodies and refuse to treat that as a thing to hide or apologize for in formal spaces. The construction is clean and the silhouette reads as genuinely elegant.
cultural_context: Popular among TESSERA-adjacent social circles and geneware-positive communities. Wearing this gown in a conservative corporate environment can be a deliberate statement. In mixed-modification social spaces it is simply correct formal wear.
story_hooks: A client orders the gown for a formal event and specifies wing-slit dimensions that don't match any standard TESSERA modification profile — whatever they had done, it wasn't done through official channels.
The gown becomes a minor flashpoint at a Tier 4 corporate gala when a guest's decorative wings are larger than the venue's fire-safety exemption allows. Security is called. The guest does not leave.
Someone commissions the gown for a synthetic being attending their first public formal event — the first time the synthetic has worn something chosen for them rather than assigned.

physical_description.visual_profile: A floor-length formal gown with an architectural silhouette that celebrates rather than conceals bodily modification. The garment reads as haute couture with a defiant edge—elegant without apology, structured without rigidity. Two vertical slit channels frame the upper back like intentional design rather than accommodation, creating a striking negative-space pattern down the spine. The overall impression is of a wearer who has claimed space in formal society on their own terms.
physical_description.fit: Tailored through the bodice and waist with a graceful A-line skirt that allows freedom of movement. The structure is precise without being restrictive; the dorsal panel system sits flush against the body without compression. The gown accommodates winged modifications naturally while maintaining a sleek silhouette for unmodified wearers.
physical_description.primary_material: High-grade silk-analog synth-fabric with the weight and drape of natural silk but enhanced durability and thermal regulation. The reinforced slit channels use a ballistic microweave for structural integrity.
physical_description.texture: Smooth and lustrous across the main body with a subtle sheen that catches light. The bias-cut trim framing the dorsal slits is slightly ribbed for contrast and grip. Overall surface is pristine and refined with subtle structural quilting at stress points.
physical_description.color_scheme: Available in eight colorways; typical palette includes deep jewel tones (sapphire, emerald, amethyst), neutral elegance (charcoal, ivory, platinum), and statement shades (blood red, gold-black). Contrasting bias-trim in complementary or contrasting metallics. Optional bioluminescent trim in cyan, violet, or soft gold adds an ethereal shimmer to evening wear.
physical_description.closures: Invisible magnetic snaps concealed along the rear bodice seam and a side-zip closure that runs from hip to armpit. The slit channels feature optional friction-fit reinforcement clips that can be engaged or left open depending on the wearer's modification presentation.
distinctive_features: Twin reinforced dorsal slit channels from mid-shoulder-blade to hip with contrasting bias-cut framing
Intentional architectural negative space that frames spinal/dorsal modifications as design feature rather than accommodation
Tail-accommodation standard at rear hem with reinforced cutaway
Hidden interior pockets at side seams
Optional bioluminescent trim upgrade compatible with subcutaneous bio-LED implants
Orvana Atelier signature hallmark embossed on interior waistband
Thermal-regulation micro-mesh integrated into side panels
physical_description.tier_indicator: Upper Tier 3 / Lower Tier 2 luxury aspiration—expensive enough to signal investment and intentionality, accessible enough for working-modified professionals to save toward
physical_description.cultural_context: Signals TESSERA-adjacent social circles, geneware-positive identity, and refusal to hide bodily modification in formal spaces. Wearing this in conservative corpo environments is a deliberate statement of autonomy; in mixed-modification social spaces it is simply correct formal wear. Popular among modified artists, mid-level corpo rebels, and high-status street culture figures.
physical_description.condition_typical: When new: pristine and structured. When worn: broken-in at stress points with a soft patina developing on the silk-analog. Maintained pieces show no wear; heavily-used pieces may develop subtle creasing along the dorsal channels from repeated modification flexing—a mark of authenticity.
